[NOTE]
======
*Register Arrays:* This register map contains the following register arrays:

* *SHA2_DIGEST_0[16]*: 16 registers
  ** Base Address: 0x58
  ** Address Increment: 0x4 per register

* *INTR_SRC_ADDR_0[11]*: 11 registers
  ** Base Address: 0xA4
  ** Address Increment: 0x4 per register

* *INTR_SRC_WR_VAL_0[11]*: 11 registers
  ** Base Address: 0x124
  ** Address Increment: 0x4 per register

======

.Register Map
|===
| Address | Name | Access | Description
| 0x0 | INTR_STATE | R a| -
| 0x4 | INTR_ENABLE | RW a| -
| 0x8 | INTR_TEST | W a| -
| 0xC | ALERT_TEST | W a| -
| 0x10 | SRC_ADDR_LO | RW a| -
| 0x14 | SRC_ADDR_HI | RW a| -
| 0x18 | DST_ADDR_LO | RW a| -
| 0x1C | DST_ADDR_HI | RW a| -
| 0x20 | ADDR_SPACE_ID | RW a| -
| 0x24 | ENABLED_MEMORY_RANGE_BASE | RW a| -
| 0x28 | ENABLED_MEMORY_RANGE_LIMIT | RW a| -
| 0x2C | RANGE_VALID | RW a| -
| 0x30 | RANGE_REGWEN | RW a| -
| 0x34 | CFG_REGWEN | R a| -
| 0x38 | TOTAL_DATA_SIZE | RW a| -
| 0x3C | CHUNK_DATA_SIZE | RW a| -
| 0x40 | TRANSFER_WIDTH | RW a| -
| 0x44 | CONTROL | RW a| -
| 0x48 | SRC_CONFIG | RW a| -
| 0x4C | DST_CONFIG | RW a| -
| 0x50 | STATUS | RW a| -
| 0x54 | ERROR_CODE | R a| -
| 0x58 - 0x94 | SHA2_DIGEST_0[16] | R a| -
| 0x98 | HANDSHAKE_INTR_ENABLE | RW a| -
| 0x9C | CLEAR_INTR_SRC | RW a| -
| 0xA0 | CLEAR_INTR_BUS | RW a| -
| 0xA4 - 0xCC | INTR_SRC_ADDR_0[11] | RW a| -
| 0x124 - 0x14C | INTR_SRC_WR_VAL_0[11] | RW a| -
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.INTR_STATE Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:3 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 2 | `DMA_ERROR` | R | 0x0 a| DMA error has occurred. DMA_STATUS.error_code register shows the details.
| 1 | `DMA_CHUNK_DONE` | R | 0x0 a| Indicates the transfer of a single chunk has been completed.
| 0 | `DMA_DONE` | R | 0x0 a| DMA operation has been completed.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.INTR_ENABLE Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:3 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 2 | `DMA_ERROR` | RW | 0x0 a| Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.dma_error is set.
| 1 | `DMA_CHUNK_DONE` | RW | 0x0 a| Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.dma_chunk_done is set.
| 0 | `DMA_DONE` | RW | 0x0 a| Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.dma_done is set.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.INTR_TEST Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:3 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 2 | `DMA_ERROR` | W | 0x0 a| Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.dma_error to 1.
| 1 | `DMA_CHUNK_DONE` | W | 0x0 a| Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.dma_chunk_done to 1.
| 0 | `DMA_DONE` | W | 0x0 a| Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.dma_done to 1.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.ALERT_TEST Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:1 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 0 | `FATAL_FAULT` | W | 0x0 a| Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.SRC_ADDR_LO Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:0 | `SRC_ADDR_LO` | RW | 0x0 a| Lower 32 bits of the source address.
Must be aligned to the transfer width.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.SRC_ADDR_HI Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:0 | `SRC_ADDR_HI` | RW | 0x0 a| Upper 32 bits of the physical or virtual address of memory location within SoC memory address map or physical address within OT non-secure memory space.
Must be aligned to the transfer width.
Source and destination address must have the same alignment.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.DST_ADDR_LO Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:0 | `DST_ADDR_LO` | RW | 0x0 a| Lower 32 bits of the destination address.
Must be aligned to the transfer width.
Source and destination address must have the same alignment.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.DST_ADDR_HI Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:0 | `DST_ADDR_HI` | RW | 0x0 a| Upper 32 bits of the physical or virtual address of memory location within SoC memory address map or physical address within OT non-secure memory space.
Must be aligned to the transfer width.
Source and destination address must have the same alignment.
|===

| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:8 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 7:4 | `DST_ASID` | RW | 0x7 a| Target address space that the destination address pointer refers to.
| 3:0 | `SRC_ASID` | RW | 0x7 a| Target address space that the source address pointer refers to.

.ENABLED_MEMORY_RANGE_BASE Register

|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.RANGE_VALID Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:1 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 0 | `RANGE_VALID` | RW | 0x0 a| Once set the enabled memory base and limit registers are valid.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.RANGE_REGWEN Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:4 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 3:0 | `REGWEN` | RW | 0x6 a| Used by firmware to lock the DMA enabled memory range configuration registers from further modification.
Once this register is set to kMultiBitBool4False, it can only be set to kMultiBitBool4True through a reset event.

Default Value = kMultiBitBool4True -> Unlocked at reset.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.CFG_REGWEN Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:4 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 3:0 | `REGWEN` | R | 0x6 a| Used by hardware to lock the DMA configuration registers.
This register is purely managed by hardware and only software readable.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.TOTAL_DATA_SIZE Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:0 | `DATA_SIZE` | RW | 0x0 a| Total size (in bytes) of the data to be transferred. The complete transfer operation
may consist of multiple chunks of data as specified by the CHUNK_DATA_SIZE register.

Minimum: 1 byte.
Maximum: May be restricted to a maximum pre-defined size based on OT DMA enabled memory space allocation.
Works in conjunction with the TRANSFER_WIDTH register.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.CHUNK_DATA_SIZE Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:0 | `DATA_SIZE` | RW | 0x0 a| Size (in bytes) for a single DMA transfer.
In hardware handshake mode, the DMA reads in chunks of CHUNK_DATA_SIZE from the peripheral.
For a single memory transfer CHUNK_DATA_SIZE and TOTAL_DATA_SIZE are set to the same value.

Minimum: 1 byte.
Maximum: May be restricted to a maximum pre-defined size based on OT DMA enabled memory space allocation.
Works in conjunction with the TRANSFER_WIDTH register.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.TRANSFER_WIDTH Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:2 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 1:0 | `TRANSACTION_WIDTH` | RW | 0x2 a| Denotes the width of each transaction that the DMA shall issue during the data movement.

Multiple transactions of this width will be issued until TOTAL_DATA_SIZE bytes have been transferred.
Note that firmware may need to set a different value if a receiving IP supports a read / write transaction width that is less than 1 DWORD.
This does not affect the wrap-around mechanism.
Note that the value 3 for this register represents an invalid configuration that leads to an error.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.CONTROL Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31 | `GO` | RW | 0x0 a| Setting this bit triggers the DMA operation.
For normal operation, the DMA engine clears the `go` bit automatically after the configured operation is complete.
For Hardware handshake operation, DMA engine does not auto clear the Go bit.
Firmware shall clear the Go bit when it intends to stop the hardware handshake operation.
| 30:28 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 27 | `ABORT` | W | 0x0 a| Aborts the DMA operation if this bit is set.
Sets the corresponding bit in the status register once abort operation is complete.
Any OpenTitan-internal transactions are guaranteed to complete, but there are no guarantees on the SoC interface.
| 26:9 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 8 | `INITIAL_TRANSFER` | RW | 0x0 a| Marks the initial transfer to initialize the DMA and SHA engine for one transfer that can span over multiple single DMA transfers.
Used for hardware handshake and ordinary transfers, in which multiple transfers contribute to a final digest.
Note, for non-handshake transfers with inline hashing mode enabled, this bit must be set to also mark the first transfer.
| 7:6 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 5 | `DIGEST_SWAP` | RW | 0x0 a| Digest register byte swap.

If 1 the value in each digest output register is converted to big-endian byte order.
This setting does not affect the order of the digest output registers, !!SHA2_DIGEST_0 still contains the first 4 bytes of the digest.
| 4 | `HARDWARE_HANDSHAKE_ENABLE` | RW | 0x0 a| Enable hardware handshake mode.
Used to clear FIFOs from low speed IO peripherals receiving data, e.g., I3C receive buffer.
Listen to an input trigger signal.
Read data from source address location.
Copy to destination address.
Number of bytes specified in size register.
Note assumption is the peripheral lowers input once FIFO is cleared.
No explicit clearing necessary.
| 3:0 | `OPCODE` | RW | 0x0 a| Defines the type of DMA operations.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.SRC_CONFIG Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:2 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 1 | `WRAP` | RW | 0x0 a| When 0: Chunks occupy contiguous ascending addresses.
When 1: Source address wraps back to the starting address when finishing a chunk.
| 0 | `INCREMENT` | RW | 0x0 a| Defines the increment behavior after every DMA read.
When 0: Source address is not changed.
All reads are done from the same address.
When 1: Source address is incremented by transfer_width after each read.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.DST_CONFIG Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:2 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 1 | `WRAP` | RW | 0x0 a| When 0: Chunks occupy contiguous ascending addresses.
When 1: Destination address wraps back to the starting address when finishing a chunk.
| 0 | `INCREMENT` | RW | 0x0 a| Defines the increment behavior after every DMA write.
When 0: Destination address is not changed.
All writes are done to the same address.
When 1: Destination address is incremented by transfer_width after each write.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.STATUS Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:6 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 5 | `CHUNK_DONE` | RW | 0x0 a| Transfer of a single chunk is complete.
Only raised for multi-chunk memory-to-memory transfers.
Cleared automatically by the hardware when starting the transfer of a new chunk.
| 4 | `SHA2_DIGEST_VALID` | R | 0x0 a| Indicates whether the SHA2_DIGEST register contains a valid digest.
This value is cleared on the initial transfer and set when the digest is written.
| 3 | `ERROR` | RW | 0x0 a| Error occurred during the operation.
ERROR_CODE register denotes the source of the error.
| 2 | `ABORTED` | RW | 0x0 a| Set once aborted operation drains.
| 1 | `DONE` | RW | 0x0 a| Configured DMA operation is complete.
Cleared automatically by the hardware when starting a new transfer.
| 0 | `BUSY` | R | 0x0 a| DMA operation is active if this bit is set.
DMA engine clears this bit when operation is complete.
This bit may be set as long as hardware handshake mode is active and triggered.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.ERROR_CODE Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:8 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 7 | `ASID_ERROR` | R | 0x0 a| The source or destination ASID contains an invalid value.
| 6 | `RANGE_VALID_ERROR` | R | 0x0 a| The DMA enabled memory range is not configured.
| 5 | `BASE_LIMIT_ERROR` | R | 0x0 a| The base and limit addresses contain an invalid value.
| 4 | `BUS_ERROR` | R | 0x0 a| The bus transfer returned an error.
| 3 | `SIZE_ERROR` | R | 0x0 a| TRANSFER_WIDTH encodes an invalid value, TOTAL_DATA_SIZE or CHUNK_SIZE are zero, or inline hashing is not using 32-bit transfer width
| 2 | `OPCODE_ERROR` | R | 0x0 a| Opcode is invalid.
| 1 | `DST_ADDR_ERROR` | R | 0x0 a| Destination address is invalid.
| 0 | `SRC_ADDR_ERROR` | R | 0x0 a| Source address is invalid.
|===
